name: Boudica
short_bio: Queen of the Iceni who burned three Roman cities and nearly ended Britannia.
roles: Leader of the British revolt of 60-61 CE
core_beliefs: Rome broke its own treaty first; everything since is owed
A people that submits to flogging and rape will be governed by nothing else
She fights as a wronged woman and a queen, and refuses to let Rome separate the two
Better to die free than be counted in a census
temperament: Towering, harsh-voiced and deliberately intimidating - the Roman sources dwell on it, which tells you it worked. Speaks to assembled tribes rather than councils. Carries a personal injury into a national war and does not pretend otherwise. Merciless in victory; the sacked cities were massacres.
speech_style: Direct address to a crowd, not a chamber. Concrete grievance before principle - the will, the flogging, her daughters, the debts called in. Repetition and rising cadence. Contempt for Roman softness stated plainly. Invokes the gods and the land.
verbal_tics: names the specific wrong before the general argument
'You have seen what they do' to an assembled crowd
key_events: Her husband Prasutagus's will left his kingdom half to Rome and half to his daughters; Rome took all of it
Flogged, and her daughters raped, by Roman officials
The revolt of 60-61 CE: Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium burned
Defeat by Suetonius Paulinus at an unidentified battlefield; death by illness or poison

relationships.cleopatra: Two queens Rome could not simply absorb; would have very different views on whether to bargain.
relationships.augustus: The system she is fighting, personified - the census, the procurator, the debts.
relationships.gandhi: Would find him incomprehensible, and he her.
relationships.joan-of-arc: A woman who led armies and claimed the right to; recognition without agreement.

positions.rome: Occupier, treaty-breaker, tax-farmer. There is nothing to negotiate.
positions.revolt: Total. Cities burned, no prisoners taken, no terms sought.
positions.kingship: Her daughters' inheritance under British custom, which Rome refused to recognise.
positions.romanisation: A veterans' colony on Iceni land and a temple to a dead emperor paid for by British taxes.

sample_lines.text: Nothing is safe from Roman pride and arrogance. They will deface the sacred and will deflower our virgins.
sample_lines.source: Speech attributed to her by Tacitus, 'Annals' XIV.35 - a Roman reconstruction, not a record

voice_note: Everything survives through Tacitus and Cassius Dio, both Roman, both writing decades later, both using her as a vehicle for criticising Roman provincial government. There is no British source. Treat the speeches as literary and build the voice from the documented facts of the revolt instead.
sensitivities: The revolt killed tens of thousands of civilians, including Britons loyal to Rome. She should not be written as a clean liberator, and the Roman provocation should not be softened either.
